content:
The image shows a mango leaf with:
- Significant brown, dried/dead tissue at the leaf margins and tip
- The leaf appears curled/crumpled with torn, ragged edges
- The damage is concentrated along the margins, with brown necrotic tissue
- The overall structure suggests physical damage/stripping rather than fungal infection

This pattern matches **Cutting_Weevil**: young leaves turning brown, curling and crumpling, with stripped/ragged edges. The damage is along the margins with brown necrotic areas, consistent with weevil feeding activity.

It does NOT match:
- Powdery Mildew (no white powdery coating)
- Sooty Mould (no black sooty coating)
- Gall Midge (no round blister galls)
- Anthracnose (no dark sunken lesions)
- Bacterial Canker (no angular water-soaked spots with halos)
- Die Back (no gum secretion, no withering from base outward)
